newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures called up on Iraq sanctions fears.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures called up on Iraq sanctions fears.

text.p: IPE oil futures were expected to jump when trade begins on Monday after the U.N. Security Council adopted a resolution at the weekend threatening Iraq with further sanctions if Baghdad blocks arms inspections.
Brokers said they anticipated gas oil starting $1.50-$2 higher than its Friday close of $158.50, while August Brent should rise some 20 cents from the pre-weekend finish of $17.67
"The possible threat of sanctions has bulled up the U.S. (ACCESS) market and we should follow," said one broker.
August WTI was up 20 cents on Monday in out of hours trading, while SIMEX Brent was also indicated higher
"I think we saw a firm base hit last week on the gas oil, when buying kicked in below $159, so hopefully we will be able to hold that," said one gas oil broker.
London brokers said their clients were already putting in buy orders on the back of the new Security Council threats.

The U.N. resolution spoke of the council's "firm intention to impose additional measures," on Iraq if it blocks arms inspections. It also suspended regular 60 day reviews of current sanctions until the end of October.
The Security Council move came after Iraq barred U.N. investigators from three sensitive sites earlier in June.
